title: How to Split Your Savings Between 401(k), Roth IRA, HSA, and Brokerage
description: The 'Investment Waterfall': A step-by-step guide to filling your tax-advantaged buckets efficiently.
content:
When you have money to invest, the first question is 'Where do I put it?' The US tax code offers a menu of accounts—401(k), Roth IRA, HSA, Traditional IRA, and Taxable Brokerage—each with unique rules, limits, and tax benefits. Choosing the wrong account order can cost you hundreds of thousands of dollars in taxes over your lifetime. The optimal strategy is to fill these buckets in a specific mathematical order, known as the 'Investment Waterfall,' to capture free money first, tax-free growth second, and liquidity third.

Key Takeaways

  • Priority 1: The Match. Always contribute enough to your 401(k) to get the full employer match. This is a guaranteed 50-100% return. Never skip this.
  • Priority 2: The Triple Tax Advantage. If eligible, max out the Health Savings Account (HSA). It beats the Roth IRA because it is tax-deductible going in AND tax-free coming out.
  • Priority 3: Tax-Free Growth. Max out the Roth IRA ($7,000). You want tax-free money in retirement to control your tax bracket.
  • Priority 4: The Spillover. Once tax shelters are full, use a Taxable Brokerage account for liquidity and early retirement bridging.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The 2025 contribution limits are: 401(k) $23,500; IRA $7,000; HSA $4,300 (Self). High earners can also use the 'Mega Backdoor Roth' strategy to stuff an additional ~$30k into their 401(k) if their plan allows it.

The Waterfall Visualization

Think of your money flowing down a series of buckets. You only move to the next bucket when the current one is full or optimized.

Bucket 1: The Employer Match (Free Money)

Action: Contribute 3-6% of salary to 401(k).

Why: Instant 100% ROI. Risk-free. This is the most profitable investment you will ever make.

Bucket 2: The HSA (The Super-IRA)

Action: Max out ($4,300).

Why: It is the only account that avoids FICA tax (if payroll deducted), Income tax, and Capital Gains tax. It acts as a Medical 401(k).

Bucket 3: Roth IRA (The Tax Hedge)

Action: Max out ($7,000).

Why: Tax-free growth. Also, you can withdraw contributions penalty-free at any time, making it a backup emergency fund.

Bucket 4: Remaining 401(k) (The Tax Break)

Action: Fill the rest of the $23,500 limit.

Why: Lowers your current year tax bill significantly.

Bucket 5: Taxable Brokerage (The Liquid Fund)

Action: Unlimited.

Why: Total liquidity. No age restrictions. Use this for a house, car, or retiring at 45.

Tactical Tips

  1. Automate the Cascade: Set your direct deposit to fill Bucket 1 and 2. Set an auto-transfer from your bank to fill Bucket 3 on payday.
  2. High Fee Warning: If your 401(k) has terrible fees (expense ratios > 1%), only do Bucket 1 (Match). Then skip to Bucket 3 (Roth IRA) where you control the fees. Go back to the 401(k) only after the IRA is full.
  3. The 'One Fund' Portfolio: You can hold the exact same fund (e.g., Target Date Index) in all four accounts to keep your asset allocation simple.
  4. Income Limits: If you earn too much for a Roth IRA (>$165k), use the 'Backdoor Roth' strategy to fill Bucket 3 legally.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I skip the HSA?

Only if you don't have a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP). If you have a PPO, you aren't eligible for an HSA. Skip to Bucket 3.

Is Brokerage better than 401(k)?

Only if you need the money in < 5 years. The tax drag on a brokerage account (paying taxes on dividends every year) slows down growth compared to the tax-deferred 401(k).

What about debt?

Insert 'High Interest Debt Payoff' between Bucket 1 and Bucket 2. Never invest in an HSA/IRA while holding 25% credit card debt. Get the match, then kill the debt.
